title: An Extended-Reality App Using Motion Capture for Bending-Active Structure
summary: Connecting measured physical positions, an adaptive digital model and XR guidance for the assembly of bending-active bamboo modules.
introduction: Natural materials do not always behave like a predetermined digital model. This collaborative study explored how motion capture could bring conditions measured during assembly back into the design process, then return an updated model to an XR application.
context: MAS in Architecture and Digital Fabrication, ETH Zürich · 2024 research project

context.title: Let physical conditions inform the model.
paragraphs: The project investigated the gap between a designed form and the changing conditions encountered while bending and joining bamboo. A fixed overlay can describe where a part should go, while the material and its contact positions may still require adjustment.

The team explored a feedback loop between physical measurement, computational modelling and assembly guidance. The research used modular bending-active geometry so that changes could be considered at the level of a plane, a control point or a length parameter.

method.title: Measure. Adapt. Guide.
paragraphs: Reflective markers and an OptiTrack / Motive / NatNet workflow supplied position information. Within Rhino and Grasshopper, Python and Kangaroo supported the adaptive model. The project extended an existing COMPAS XR workflow, using MQTT and Firebase to exchange geometry and interaction state with a Unity application.
The three steps below describe the team's intended data flow. They are an explanatory diagram of the archived research, not a live tracking connection or a simulation running on this page.

prototype.title: From module selection to assembly guidance.
paragraphs: The prototype connected module selection with measurement and assembly controls. The research distinguished adapting the global form, assembling an individual module and joining modules into the larger structure.

The recording frame preserves an actual interface state. It does not establish that every interaction worked reliably, nor does it assign all interface, geometry or fabrication work to one researcher.

contributionNote: These contributions are supported by source-code changes and Git history. The research, overall application, geometry and fabrication are collaborative work with Wataru Nomura; the sources do not resolve every task between the two researchers. The tracking SDKs and upstream COMPAS XR framework are third-party foundations.
limitations: The research report records update delays, virtual-to-physical registration differences and image-target instability that remained unresolved within the study.
No user-study metrics or controlled usability evaluation were established. Personal assembly experiences are not presented here as a measured productivity gain.
The archived geometry snapshot has unresolved physical-unit, orientation and module-grouping details. It is not used here to invent an exploded assembly, a deformation sequence or a new simulation.
This case documents a 2024 research prototype. The original app and tracking hardware have not been re-run or benchmarked for this website.
